subject: Window smoothing and noisy CN data

messages.author: 4ee2182519091cbd
messages.subject: Window smoothing and noisy CN data
parts:
Dear all:

First off, like many others already I would like to thank you for
aroma.affymetrix.

I'm just starting to learn how to use the software, and I've gotten
through the full CN analysis of 96 Affymetrix 6.0 chips (which took a
while!). The software works wonderfully and I have my results.

My question: I have *very* noisy data (and this is not aroma's
fault!). The noise comes from extra amplification steps. The scale of
the noise is impressive, but there still is an average copy number
result, somewhere around 0.3 that seems to be consistent in some
chips. In others, the CN data is fragmented (many different CNs abound
on every chromosome) which looks like it's an effect of the noise.


Therefore, I'd like to increase a smoothing window in the process. I
apologize if this is already mentioned somewhere; can you point me if
possible to a way to increase the smoothing window? I'm not interested
in small CNs -- I'd be happy with large averaged regions as I'm
interested in aneuploidy on a chromosomal scale.

Thank you!

> through the full CN analysis of 96 Affymetrix 6.0 chips (which took a
> while!). The software works wonderfully and I have my results.
>
> My question: I have *very* noisy data (and this is not aroma's
> fault!). The noise comes from extra amplification steps. The scale of
> the noise is impressive, but there still is an average copy number
> result, somewhere around 0.3 that seems to be consistent in some
> chips. In others, the CN data is fragmented (many different CNs abound
> on every chromosome) which looks like it's an effect of the noise.
>
>
> Therefore, I'd like to increase a smoothing window in the process. I
> apologize if this is already mentioned somewhere; can you point me if
> possible to a way to increase the smoothing window? I'm not interested
> in small CNs -- I'd be happy with large averaged regions as I'm
> interested in aneuploidy on a chromosomal scale.

I don't think you want to smooth data before passing it on to a
segmentation method, but rather you want the segmentation method to
deal with the noise. For both the CbsModel and the GladModel
segmentation classes, you, via fit(), can pass additional arguments to
the internal segmentation functions, that is, to segment() of DNAcopy
and glad() of GLAD, respectively. See help for those function in the
corresponding package.

I second guess you that you are using the CbsModel for segmentation,
correct? (please provide complete script next time). I haven't
played with the tuning parameters for segment(), but you can tell to
post-prune identified regions by:

cbs <- CbsModel(cesN);
fit(cbs, arrays=1:3, chromosomes=4:6, undo.splits="prune");

There are several tuning arguments, so you'll have to try different
settings. I hope you find a setup that works for you. For more help
on those, please ask the authors of the segmentation package you use.

Also, I tried, and you can even pass these parameters via the
process() of ChromosomeExplorer, e.g.

ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(cbs);
process(ce, arrays=1:3, chromosomes=4:6, undo.splits="prune");

Note, in both cases, if you want to refit already fitted
segmentations, you can do that by adding argument 'force=TRUE'. An
alternative, at least when you play with different settings and want
to keep everything, you can add your own custom tags to the CbsModel
output, e.g.

cbs <- CbsModel(cesN, tags="*,prune");
fit(cbs, arrays=1:3, chromosomes=4:6, undo.splits="prune");

cbs <- CbsModel(cesN, tags="*,prune=0.10");
fit(cbs, arrays=1:3, chromosomes=4:6, undo.splits="prune", undo.prune=0.10);

etc. Please feel free to share what you learn on this mailing list.
If you find something useful, we can add a paragraph on this to one of
the vignettes. If you're really serious about it, we can add a
complete vignette illustrate what different settings does to the
segmentation.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.author: 4ee2182519091cbd
messages.subject: Re: Window smoothing and noisy CN data
parts:
For the record, to process the 96 Affy 6.0 chips, I exactly followed
the Total Copy Number Analysis (5.0 & 6.0) vignette. It was very
helpful and everything worked perfectly.

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0

I followed the vignette exactly, for the non-paired CNR case (common
reference as robust average across samples).

On my Macbook Pro, the TCNA of the 96 Affy 6.0 chips was going to take
about a week to process the data (or so the output was telling me), so
I switched over to a newer Windows server and it only took a day or so
of aggregate time. The install and processing on the Windows server
was seamless.

Deanne
